answer: The wander detector writes to grove, and wharf reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, and thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 272 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 264 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 25 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
